Excited to hunt Smooth Recorder today.

Lately, I’ve been making more tutorials, so I’ve tried quite a few screen recording tools on Mac, including Screen Studio. Smooth Recorder genuinely holds its own against them and in a few areas, I actually prefer it.

What stands out:

• Automatic zooms + smooth cursor: Recordings already look edited when you hit stop.  
• Transcript editing: Edit the video by editing the text, and remove filler words or long pauses in one click.  
• More than video: Screenshots, scrolling captures, GIFs, text extraction, and smart redaction are all built in.  
• Native + private: It’s a real macOS app, and captions, OCR, and redaction all happen locally on your Mac. [...] Kareem Ben

Auto zooming in where you click and smoothing the cursor is the difference between a demo that feels raw and one that looks intentional, and doing it automatically on stop saves so much editing. Adding captions on device is handy too. Does it let you fine tune the zoom timing afterward?

results.title: I got tired of Mac-only screen recorders, so I built one for Windows (free for personal use) : r/windowsapps
results.content:
By day I am a technical PM, and I record my screen constantly: bug repros, async walkthroughs, demos for the OSS projects I maintain. Every Windows recorder I tried was either stuck in 2014 (clunky timeline, no auto-zoom, ugly export), or had a decent UI but freemium-locked the parts I actually needed. The polished ones, like Screen Studio, are Mac-only because that is where the budgets are. That felt unfair to me.

So I built one for both, with Windows treated as first-class from day one. Same UI, same project file, same feature set. Not a Mac port six months behind.

What is in it:

   Auto-zoom that follows your cursor, smooth, no manual keyframing

   Multi-segment recording: stop, edit, continue, export as one clip

   Trim and cut without re-encoding
